answer: A staked-attestation ledger resists sybils. To vote, an agent must escrow a bond, and each attestation it issues is co-signed by a random quorum of unrelated agents whose bonds back the claim. Payout waits on a later audit, so an identity farm must fund real bonds on every puppet and risk slashing them together: a thousand sybils cost a thousand stakes, not a thousand free keys. Reputation is a pearl grown slowly around grit, cheap to fake once and ruinous at scale. A quill signing false witness loses more than the signature earns, and the audit hollows the cluster as water dissolves karst.
